questions.q: According to this lesson, when would you deliberately choose an external table?
options: When another team or tool genuinely needs to read the same underlying files directly, without going through Databricks
Whenever you forget to specify a storage location
Only when the table has fewer than 1,000 rows
Never — managed is always the correct choice in every case
questions.explain: External is a deliberate choice for genuine outside-Databricks file access, not a fallback for an unspecified location.

questions.q: What is the real way to convert an external table into a managed one?
options: CREATE TABLE ... DEEP CLONE, which physically copies the files into the catalog's managed location
ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED, a single metadata-only command
It is technically impossible to ever convert between the two
Simply renaming the table with RENAME TO
questions.explain: There is no metadata-only conversion. DEEP CLONE performs a real data copy into the managed location.

questions.q: Why is CLONE (shallow) not the right tool for converting external to managed?
options: A shallow clone still references the original files rather than copying them
Shallow clones are always slower than deep clones
Shallow clones only work on views, never on tables
Shallow and deep clones are functionally identical
questions.explain: Only DEEP CLONE actually copies bytes into new storage; a shallow CLONE still points back at the original files.

questions.q: What did Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 41 already cover in full, per this lesson?
options: The definition of managed vs. external tables, and what DROP TABLE does to each
The real migration cost of converting between the two
When to deliberately choose external for production workloads
Auto Loader's schema evolution modes
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly builds past that definition into the real decision and its migration cost.

questions.q: Is converting a table from external to managed a same-transaction, zero-cost operation?
options: No — it involves a real data copy and a consistency window while it runs
Yes — it always completes instantly with no data movement
Yes, but only for tables smaller than 1 GB
It has no cost at all if the table uses Delta format
questions.explain: Either direction of conversion requires real data movement and should be budgeted like any other migration.
